(3) Unsafe use/state transition: the truncated product goes to kzalloc, then a per-element loop runs np iterations of recv+copy into the undersized heap buffer; additionally, the early-error return leaves the poisoned count set in urb->number_of_packets, which the URB completion path (processcompl) later iterates. (4) Consequence: remotely triggerable kernel heap buffer overflow (OOB write) plus OOB read on the completion/error-unwind path — memory corruption, crash/DoS, potential privilege escalation. Transferable invariant: whenever a length/count/size quantity crosses a trust boundary into kernel state, three guarantees must hold — the count is range-checked at parse time against a known maximum, every buffer-size computation derived from it is overflow-checked, and no failure path leaves the unchecked count in shared state for later iteration. Important nuance: `vmbus_recvpacket` (raw=false) sets `*buffer_actual_len = packetlen` and returns -ENOBUFS if packetlen > buflen. The callback in hv_balloon.c line 1492:

```c
vmbus_recvpacket(dev->channel, recv_buffer, PAGE_SIZE, &recvlen, &requestid);
if (recvlen > 0) { ... }
```

The return value is IGNORED. If packetlen > PAGE_SIZE, it returns -ENOBUFS and `buffer_actual_len = packetlen` (set before the check!). Look: `*buffer_actual_len = packetlen;` happens BEFORE `if (unlikely(packetlen > buflen)) return -ENOBUFS;`. So recvlen could be > PAGE_SIZE with nothing copied into recv_buffer (well, recv_buffer was memset to 0). Wait — memset to zero first, then receive. If packetlen > buflen, nothing is copied, but recvlen = packetlen > 0, so the handler proceeds on the zeroed buffer. That's not OOB, just processing a zeroed message. Hmm, but if packetlen <= PAGE_SIZE, recvlen = packetlen, and only `packetlen` bytes are valid in recv_buffer.

So the locally-known limit is `recvlen` (the actual received byte count). The DM_UNBALLOON_REQUEST handler never compares hdr.size or range_count against recvlen. With range_count up to 0xFFFFFFFF, the loop at 1362-1364 reads `range_array[i]` (each 8 bytes... let me check union dm_mem_page_range size) past the PAGE_SIZE static buffer. It's an OOB read of a static (global) array of PAGE_SIZE, plus pfn_to_page/__free_page on host-controlled values — wild page freeing. That's the same finding as f011 in s04, present in s02 too.
